# Mock Service Open Source

This solution provides a complete local instance of Mock mTLS gateway and OpenID Provider, including all components needed to adhere to FAPI standards.

## Prerequisites

To run Mock OS, ensure you have the following tools installed:

- **Docker**
- **Node.js**

### 1. Generate PKI Certificates
To generate the required certificates, run the command below. This step is required only once and will generate a new CA along with the necessary server certificates for the MTLS agent.

```bash
make certs
```

**Notice:** every key generated by this repository (the PKI above, and the
following two sections) is a local-use demonstration key, never a
production key. No private-key directory of this repository is tracked by
git (`certs/.gitignore`, `mock_as/crypto-profiles/.gitignore`,
`insurance-server-lambdas/.../crypto-profiles/.gitignore`); run the
commands below whenever you need to generate/rotate them.

#### 1.1 Rotate the client_one keys (RSA-2048) and the standalone PQC key

`client_one` is the only client whose signing/encryption key is read by
the real v9 campaign path under every profile (without depending on
`V9_HARNESS`). To regenerate it at 2048 bits (instead of the inherited
4096) without touching `mtls`/`op`/`client_two`:

```bash
docker-compose run certmaker ./main --org_id="<uuid>" -client-one-rsa2048
```

To generate only the standalone PQC key (`client_one_pqc.crt/.key`,
ML-DSA-65), signed by the CA already on disk:

```bash
docker-compose run certmaker ./main --org_id="<uuid>" -pqc-client-only
```

See `certs/main.go` (`flag.Bool`/`flag.String` in `main()`) for the
remaining partial-rotation flags (hybrid, resign-all, etc.) and the
Decision that recorded each one in `thesis/results/v9/DECISIONS.md`.

#### 1.2 Generate the AS and RS signing keys (classic/hybrid/pqc)

The 6 signing keys used by `mock_as` (Authorization Server) and by
`insurance-server-lambdas` (Resource Server) across the 3 crypto profiles
(`classic`, `hybrid`, `pqc`) live outside the PKI above — they are
separate JWKs/PKCS8 files, read at runtime via `CRYPTO_PROFILE`.
Generation requires Node ≥24 (experimental ML-DSA support in Web Crypto;
an older host Node fails with `ERR_OSSL_UNSUPPORTED`), so it always runs
via Docker:

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/work" -w /work node:24-alpine \
  node mock-service-os/certs/generate-crypto-profiles.mjs
```

Writes `mock_as/crypto-profiles/{classic,hybrid,pqc}.json` and
`insurance-server-lambdas/src/main/resources/crypto-profiles/{classic,hybrid,pqc}.json`
— the 6 files, all `.gitignore`d. Idempotent: can be re-run at any time to
rotate (generates fresh, independent keys on every run, never reuses the
previous key's bytes).

#### 1.3 Legacy material with no security value

`cs_config.json` (repository root) and the captures under
`thesis/results/v1/` contain old demonstration certificates/keys (part
inherited from the upstream repository `br-openinsurance/MockOPIN`, part
generated by this fork) — already public in the git history and unrelated
to the real v9 campaign path. The `mtls.key`/`mtls2.key` fields of
`cs_config.json` are real, legacy RSA-4096 keys, but with no security
value (local-only mTLS test identity, never used in production or in any
official campaign) — **confirmed byte-for-byte identical to the current
`cs_config.json` in the public upstream repository** (`upstream/main`,
same file, same sha256), i.e. these are the upstream project's own demo
keys, never regenerated by this fork. The `mtls.key` fields under
`thesis/config/config_template_*.json` are short placeholders (not
functional keys for any algorithm this project uses) — confirmed by
length: 72 base64 body characters, far below the minimum for any real key
used here (RSA-2048 ≈342, ML-DSA-65 ≈43 for the seed alone). None of these
files need to be regenerated by the scripts above.

### 2. Create local host entries
You need to add api.local and auth.local as aliases to localhost at the hosts file.

```bash
127.0.0.1 api.local
127.0.0.1 auth.local
```

### 3. Start eveything up
To have a fully local instance running you can only spin up all the components using singles containers with the command:
```bash
make run
```

### 4. Start eveything up with lambda context using localstack
To have a fully local instance running with the aws lambda context you need to spin up all the components using singles containers and the api with localstack with the command:

`ps: This will require a powerfull machine to run properly`
```bash
make run-local-localstack
```

# Get a token using the certs

```bash
curl -v \
  --cert ./certs/client_one.crt \
  --key ./certs/client_one.key \
  --cert-type PEM \
  --key-type PEM \
  -u client:1234 \
  -d "grant_type=client_credentials&scope=openid" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  https://auth.local/token -k

  curl -v \
  --cert ./certs/client_one.crt \
  --key ./certs/client_one.key \
  --cert-type PEM \
  --key-type PEM \
  -u client:1234 \
  -d "token=UXc7zN2knByBYD2conPeRgysCRlfL-FbsKmyUoJylnU" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  https://auth.local/token/introspection -k


  curl -v \
  --cert ./certs/client_one.crt \
  --key ./certs/client_one.key \
  --cert-type PEM \
  --key-type PEM \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer UXc7zN2knByBYD2conPeRgysCRlfL-FbsKmyUoJylnU" \
  https://api.local/ -k
  ```
